subject: [PATCH v2 2/3] sched/numa: do not feed tiering promotions into task placement stats

reviews.author: Li Zhe
reviews.summary: Li Zhe agreed with Joshua's assessment that patch 2 is a fix rather than an optimization, and offered to re-send it separately after rc1 is released with proper Fixes tag and Cc stable
reviews.raw_body:
Thanks for the review.

Agreed, patch 2 is better framed as a fix.  I will check the exact
commit that introduced this path and can resend it separately with a
proper Fixes tag and Cc stable after rc1 is released.

For patches 1 and 3, I agree they are more about the tiering heuristic
and policy behavior.  I will keep them separate from the fix discussion
and continue that part together with the pghot-related discussion.

Thanks,
Zhe

reviews.author: Bharata Rao
reviews.summary: Reviewer noted that this patch cannot be an independent fix until there is an alternative provided by patch 3, and requested input from Ying Huang on why only successful promotions drove fault stats in tiering mode.
reviews.raw_body:
Currently only successful promotions feed stats to scan period update.
This change stops that and nothing updates the scan period for tiering
mode after this change.

Though the direction of the fix is right, I think this can't be an
independent fix until there is some alternative which patch 3 in this
series brings in.

Also it would be good to get a view from Ying Huang as to why only
successful promotions drove the fault stats while unsuccessful promotions
didn't in the tiering mode.

Regards,
Bharata.

reviews.author: Li Zhe
reviews.summary: Reviewer Li Zhe agreed that patch 2 should not be sent as a standalone fix without the replacement scan-period feedback path
reviews.raw_body:
Agreed, thanks for pointing this out.  Patch 2 should not be sent as a
standalone fix without the replacement scan-period feedback path.

Thanks,
Zhe

2026-10-29.patch_summary: This patch prevents tiering promotions from being fed into task placement statistics in the Linux kernel's NUMA (Non-Uniform Memory Access) balancing code. This fix addresses incorrect NUMA balancing behavior that could be visible to userspace, specifically regarding task placement and related accounting. The patch is considered a fix rather than an optimization, and it is recommended to submit it independently with a Fixes: tag and cc:stable.
